title: A bill arrives
caption: Both chambers of the National Assembly have passed the same text, and it is still not law. The power to make laws is exercised by bills passed by the Senate and the House and assented to by the President, so it comes here.

title: Thirty days
caption: The bill cannot simply be left on the desk. From the day it is presented the President has thirty days to signify one of two things: assent, or the withholding of it.

check.question: How long does the President have to decide on a bill?
check.explain: Within thirty days of a bill being presented, the President must signify either assent or the withholding of assent.

title: Assent
caption: A signature, with the people whose bill it is standing behind the chair to see it done. That is the moment the bill becomes law.

title: Or not
caption: The President can refuse. That is not the end of the bill: if the Senate and the House each pass it again by a two-thirds majority, it becomes law without this desk.

check.question: Both chambers pass a refused bill again by two-thirds. Must the President now sign it?
options: Yes — the President is then obliged to sign
No — it becomes law without the President's assent
It goes to the Supreme Court to decide
check.explain: Where assent is withheld and each House passes the bill again by a two-thirds majority, the bill becomes law and the President's assent is not required.

title: Who is signing
caption: The coat of arms and the flags are behind the chair because of what the office is. The President is three things at once: the Head of State, the Chief Executive of the Federation, and the Commander-in-Chief of its Armed Forces.

check.question: Which of these is the President not, under the Constitution?
check.explain: The President is the Head of State, the Chief Executive of the Federation and the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces. The National Assembly is a separate arm with its own presiding officers.
